title: Hermite coefficient norm bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have finite second moment under the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures. For every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the absolute value of the Hermite coefficient of $f$ indexed by $\alpha$ is at most the $L^2$ norm of $f$ under that product Gaussian measure.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ belongs to $L^2$ under the product standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$
